attempted_claim: Consider i∂_t u + Δu + |u|^4 u = 0 on I×R^3 with E(u)=½‖∇u‖²_2−⅙‖u‖⁶_6 and ground state W(x)=(1+|x|²/3)^(−1/2), −ΔW=W^5, E(W)=⅓‖∇W‖²_2. Let u_0 ∈ Ḣ¹(R³)∩L²(R³) be cylindrically symmetric, u_0(x_1,x_2,x_3)=U_0((x_1²+x_2²)^{1/2},x_3), with E(u_0)<E(W), ‖∇u_0‖_{L²}<‖∇W‖_{L²}, and axial momentum P_z(u_0)=Im∫ ū ∂_{x_3}u dx = 0. Let u:I_max×R³→C be the maximal-lifespan Ḣ¹ solution. Prove I_max=R, ‖u‖_{L^{10}_{t,x}(R×R³)}<∞, and hence scattering in Ḣ¹ in both time directions to states u_± ∈ Ḣ¹, with no additional drift, quantile-window, low-frequency-tail, or negative-regularity hypothesis on any associated compact critical element.
decisive_failure: Variational trapping and the cylindrical profile-decomposition reduction to an axially-translating critical element were established as working notes only; no unconditional scattering, rigidity, drift-bound, tightness, or regularity result was proved, and the scripted virial error model is diagnostic rather than a theorem.
